draft.title: Speed, distance and time
card: Speed is how far something travels in one unit of time. Speed \(=\) distance \(\div\) time.
Rearrange it to find the other two. Distance \(=\) speed \(\times\) time. Time \(=\) distance \(\div\) speed.
The units must match. Distance in km and time in hours gives speed in km/h. If time is in minutes and speed is in km/h, change the minutes to hours first.
A cyclist rides at 24 km/h for 2 hours. Distance \(= 24 \times 2 = 48\) km.
draft.remember: Speed is distance over time. Make the units match before you calculate.

a.q: A train travels 150 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?
a.why: Speed \(=\) distance \(\div\) time \(= 150 \div 2 = 75\) km/h. Multiplying gives 300, but that treats speed as distance times time, which is the formula for nothing here.
a.clue: Divide the distance by the time.

b.q: Mia walks at 6 km/h. How far does she walk in 30 minutes?
b.why: Change 30 minutes to 0.5 hours, then distance \(= 6 \times 0.5 = 3\) km. Using 30 without converting gives 180, which mixes minutes with km/h.
b.clue: Write the time in hours first.
